items.title: Milton Batiste Interview, 1997-02-05
items.q: INTERVIEWER: Local guy? Local, from New Orleans? [INTERVIEWEE] Well no. He came to study at Zav... He was a very popular alto saxophonist.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Oh yeah, yeah. And my aunt, one of my aunts played piano. And she taught at school. She was also, she always so became a principal. As a matter of fact, I just found out that she is the first black female, American, to graduate from Columbia University. Wow. Yeah. Her name is Angelina Stevenson Campbell. She was a Jollibee. And she used to be principal of a couple of high schools here. So she's still living. She's 93 years old now. She's. Yeah. And so, I can't think of the alto man's name, you know, like…
Local guy? Local, from New Orleans?

Well no. He came to study at Zav. He came to study music and other things. He wasn't, his home wasn't here. But he became very popular. He was a very popular alto saxophonist. Like Coleman, like, who was his name that played with alto? Duke. I'm forgetting all these people's names. Boyhood heroes too.
